0.0.n: 月 after a number names a month of the year.

0.1.n: Placed after October to make the starting time approximate.

0.2.n: Marks the starting point of the season.

0.3.n: 月 after a number names a month of the year.

0.4.n: Placed after March to make the ending time approximate.

0.5.n: Marks the endpoint of the season.

0.6.n: Casually introduces the whole October-to-March period as the topic, similar to は.

1.0.n: Names the sport whose season the speaker is describing.

1.1.n: Links マラソン to シーズン, specifying what kind of season it is.

1.2.n: An English loanword for the period when these races take place.

1.3.n: The linking form of だ used after a noun before ので.

1.4.n: Introduces the season as the reason for entering races during this period.

2.0.n: Points back to the October-to-March period and modifies 中.

2.1.n: Refers to the inside of a time period rather than a physical space.

2.2.n: Marks that period as the time frame for participating in races.

2.4.n: 回 counts occurrences, here participation in a race.

2.5.n: Connects two possible numbers of race appearances.

2.6.n: 回 counts occurrences, so 2回 indicates two race appearances.

2.7.n: Adds a minimum-like emphasis to the approximate count of one or two races.

2.8.n: Short for フルマラソン, contrasting with shorter races such as a half marathon.

2.9.n: Links フル to 大会, identifying the event as a full-marathon race.

2.10.n: 大会 means an organized competition; here it refers to a marathon event.

2.11.n: Marks the event the speaker participates in with 出る.

2.12.n: The plain nonpast form describes a regular habit here, not necessarily a future plan.

2.13.n: Casual form of という, linking the preceding description to 感じ.

2.14.n: With っていう, presents the routine as a rough description rather than a rigid commitment.

2.15.n: Politely ends the description after the noun 感じ.

2.16.n: Softens the ending and invites the listener to share the speaker's understanding.

0.lit: As for from around October until around March,
0.tip: って casually marks the entire time span as the topic.

1.tip: After a noun, な links to ので to express because it is.

2.lit: During that, at least once or twice, I enter a full-marathon race—that's the general pattern, you know.
2.tip: っていう感じです softens the statement into a rough description of the speaker's usual routine.
